**Finding submitted: IP — deviation (fallback target).**

**What I found**
- **§10.4 (p0185)** — M&I owns all programs, ideas, know-how and *any* writing or work of authorship created in performing the Services, "even if paid for by Customer" (defined as "Developed Software"), with only a partial refund/credit if M&I later sells a service derived from it. No licence back.
- **§17.2 (p0244)** — confirms Customer "has no rights" in M&I materials except use "during the Term to process its data" — i.e. our rights are term-limited, non-modifiable and non-sublicensable. Fallback fails on its material terms.
- **§17.4 (p0249)** — M&I may use Confidential Information (which expressly includes all Customer Data) for the broad "purposes contemplated by this Agreement", which is wider than processing solely to provide the Services and is not cured by the ownership sentence in 17.1.
- **§17.1 (p0243)** — Customer is sole and exclusive owner of Customer Data: favourable, not flagged. **§17.5** security and **§23.5** source-code use limits are Customer-side/neutral and out of scope for this rule.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**
1. Insert after §10.4: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business, expressly overriding §17.2 so no dangling contradiction remains.
2. Surgical insertion into §17.4 keeping every other word verbatim: "except that M&I shall use and process Customer Data solely to provide the Services".

M&I's ownership of generic programs, ideas and know-how is left intact (already-met fallback element), so no assignment reversal or collateral rewrite of the 10.4 refund mechanic is required.
